answer: Inter-arrival spacing floor. Each identity's first N actions must arrive with gaps drawn from a wide distribution; a comet of bursty clones arriving near-simultaneously trips the check and gets throttled. The bridge between fast and slow lanes requires sustained spacing over many sessions, so a ledge of cheap parallel accounts never clears it. Attacker cost: N × spacing window per identity in wall-clock time, multiplying with clone count instead of staying flat.
